text:
sam: Heads-up — ran into a weird ESM/CJS interop failure only when building for edge (Vite/Rollup target=esnext + webpack dev server also repros). Minimal app works in Node, fails in edge env (Cloudflare/Workers, Vercel Edge).

sam: Repro steps I used (super small):
1) package.json with "type": "module"
2) index.js imports the SDK with `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` then calls `Redwood.generate(...)`
3) bundle with Vite (esbuild) or Rollup and deploy to an edge runtime

sam: Error in edge console: `ReferenceError: require is not defined` but stack traces point at code inside the SDK that our build turns into CJS wrapper.

sam: Full minimal repro gist: https://gist.github.com/sam-repro/0f1a2b3c (contains vite.config, rollup.config, simple index.js) — note: this is a fake link for repro notes.

maria: Oof. Did you try forcing the SDK entry to the ESM build? Some bundlers prefer the `main` field and pick CJS.

sam: Yeah — I checked package exports: SDK publishes `exports` with `import` and `require` fields. Locally Node picks the ESM `import`, but Rollup/Vite sometimes resolve to `require` path depending on resolver plugins.

devon: Can you paste your vite.config? Vite dev server often uses native ESM but the SSR/edge build path can go through rollup plugin-commonjs conversion.

sam: vite.config.js snippet:
```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    target: 'es2020',
    ssr: true,
    rollupOptions: {
      external: [],
    },
  },
})
```

sam: When I set `build.target` to `esnext` or `modules: true` it still pulled a CJS wrapper for one internal util and that wrapper expects `require`. Edge runtime fails.

maria: Suggestion: try adding `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['redwood-inference']` and `ssr.noExternal: ['redwood-inference']`. That forces Vite to treat the package as ESM source for the SSR/edge build.

sam: tried that — `ssr.noExternal` helped for Vite (replaced CJS wrapper), but Rollup-based deploy (our CI bundling for the edge runtime) still ended up with commonjs interop.

jordan: For Rollup, check `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` config and `include` globs. If commonjs plugin runs after aliasing it can wrap ESM in a CJS shim. Also `preserveModules` can change outputs.

sam: Relevant error trace (edge console):
```
ReferenceError: require is not defined
    at eval (node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.cjs:12:34)
    at instantiateModule (edge-runtime.js:45:12)
    at ...
```

devon: Does the SDK ship a dual build? If there's a `dist/index.cjs` and `dist/index.mjs`, bundlers might still pick the wrong one. We should check the `package.json` `exports`/`module`/`main` ordering.

sam: It does. `exports` has `./package.json`, `.` with `import` -> `dist/index.mjs`, `require` -> `dist/index.cjs`.

ashley: For a quick workaround, you can alias the package to the ESM entry in your bundler config:
- Vite: `alias: { 'redwood-inference': 'redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs' }`
- Rollup: `alias({ entries: { 'redwood-inference': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs') } })`

sam: That worked locally, but need a robust fix — can't expect all customers to alias. Also types: TypeScript projects sometimes pick up `types` pointing to `dist/index.d.ts` which matches ESM, but if bundler uses CJS then typed imports are fine but runtime breaks.

maria: Could be a packaging bug: some internal submodule using `createRequire` or `require('fs')` guarded by `if (typeof window === 'undefined')` might still be present in the ESM file and bundlers can't tree-shake the guard. Edge bundles then ship `require` calls.

sam: I inspected the ESM file — there's a tiny helper that does `var require = ...` as part of a bundler output when publishing. Looks like our publish pipeline inadvertently ran a CJS emitter into the ESM bundle for small helpers.

devon: That's the smoking gun. If ESM dist contains transformed CJS helpers, edge runtimes will choke. Easy fix: ensure ESM build target emits native ESM helpers (no `require` polyfills).

jordan: Action items for SDK team: (1) audit `dist/*.mjs` for any `require` usage, (2) update rollup/tsup config to use `format: 'esm'` and avoid commonjs transform for ESM bundle, (3) publish patch with corrected exports.

sam: I'm attaching repro logs in the gist and a small Dockerfile that runs the edge-like runtime: `FROM node:18-alpine`, `npm run build`, `npx vercel dev --listen 0.0.0.0` to simulate.

ci-bot: deploy-check: build pipeline failed on the tracestate-integration job (see https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/1234) — failing test: "edge-bundle-repro".

ashley: For immediate customer-side docs, we should add a section in SDK troubleshooting: "Edge runtimes & bundlers: common gotchas" with the alias workaround and `ssr.noExternal` instructions. Also call out that ESM dist must not contain `require`.

maria: Also add a TypeScript note: if consuming with `tsconfig.moduleResolution = 'bundler'`, module resolution changes. Recommend `node` with `moduleResolution: 'node16'` for edge builds.

sam: I'll open a repo issue with the minimal repro + CI logs and link to this thread. Assigning to @devon to take the packaging fix.

devon: I'll run a clean publish locally and check artifact contents. If I see `require` in `.mjs` I'll change the builder flags.

jordan: After fix, we should add a lightweight E2E smoke test that bundles the SDK with Vite/Rollup/Vitest for an edge target and runs in a Node-compatible edge shim to catch regressions.

ashley: Agreed. Also include a small sample app in `examples/edge-sdk` demonstrating recommended vite.config and tsconfig settings.

sam: Thanks all — will follow up with the issue link. :thumbsup:
